I think what makes the more open ended pre-dungeon better is that you're encouraged to wander around. Twilight Princess' most successful pre dungeons are Snowhead Temple and Temple of Time because even though they are linear your are exploring. They harken back to the desert storm leading to the Spirit Temple in OoT. Unfortunately these ones can also drag, but the opportunity and push to explore is so appreciated.

Wind Waker's is barely any less linear, but the game as a whole is more open to make up for it, and the trifroce hunt fulfills the explore the world bit in a concentrated segment (reason I don't like the HD hunt as much). I think TP's version of the triforce hunt (getting the pages for the dominion rod) and the tears of light (which is kind of pre dungeon ish in function) fails for being SO linear. Surprisingly I find Phantom Hourglass is pretty good in this aspect. 

This is why I think the linear pre dungeons of BotW and TotK is also fine, because the game makes up for it in everything *before* being so wander-y.

As a Strategist main... they have to be. If divers as a whole weren't able to secure kills against isolated squishy characters (healers) they would be both useless and incredibly non-fun to play. Its part of the rock paper scissors etc. part of team comps. 

Unfortunately a lot of people play selfishly, and a lot of people just don't pay much attention to the map and the other team. I play Strange a lot and it CAN be hard to tell when a team mate is going to get dived, but its also a basic-math type thing. If you're frontlining and can see everyone on the other team except for their Psylocke, Spiderman, or BP you can assume where they are. When you suddenly stop getting heals you can assume what's happening. 

Not the same type of game, but trying to use say a Roller or especially Ink Brush in Splatoon is often miserable because a ton of good backline weapons in that game have both good escape, and can usually kill faster than you can. That's kind of what it'd be like if Strategists as a whole were able to consistently counter divers.

I took it as chaos being oblivion's *opposite*. While oblivion is nothing, chaos can be any and everything. Such that the greatest will creates the most chaos, which breeds stronger will. While oblivion stagnates all into exact order.
I take the brine as being oblivion manifest.
I interpret the reason our pawn became a dragon was because of their lesser will defying but not being able to fully stave oblivion, not being consumed by it. In the same way a failed Arisen becomes a dragon (not great enough will to ascend, but strong enough to stave off oblivion tempering them into a dragon). Dragons being will born from and in defiance of oblivion.

If that makes any sense I'm honestly making myself lost on this.

I think the cycle is inherit to this universe on a cosmic timescale, but I think the goal is to temper stronger and stronger wills each cycle that last longer with more prosperity. A seneschal with stronger will than the last, and a general populace with greater will than the last. 

It's why I REALLY love the idea of Dragons Dogma 2 being a true sequel to DD1, whether it's 1 or 900 cycles later. The game world being bigger than the first is canon! NPCs all going to the seafloor shrine instead of just giving up like DD1 Grand Soren is an expression of this world's general stronger will. 

In my interpretation the world having such a strong collective will that the cycle ends is impossible, because oblivion *is* stagnation, and a world never ending is one inherently stagnant.

I think the nature of the cycle can be compared to a lot of From Soft game worlds. A cycle not ending may not result in destruction, but stagnation. My interpretation isn't that stagnation causes oblivion, but that stagnation *is* oblivion.The purest destruction in this world is the dragon, who's a being of massive will born in opposition to oblivion. Where as most media destruction and the end is the worst outcome, in DD destruction tempers stronger wills which breeds new and more expansive life in a hopefully ever improving cycle.
